newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina to raise import duties half a point.
newsitem.headline: Argentina to raise import duties half a point.

text.p: Argentine import duties will soon be raised half a percentage point to finance a new import control system, Economy Minister Roque Fernandez said on Tuesday.

Fernandez told reporters that the government initially planned to raise the 3.0 percent "statistical tax" on imports to 3.5 percent, but had now changed its mind and will raise import duties from all non-Mercosur countries instead.
Argentina's partners in the Mercosur customs union are Brazil, Paraguay and Uruguay.
A government official told the state-run Telam news agency that the authorities plan to issue a decree, perhaps as soon as this week implementing the new imports control system.
Under the new rules, the customs service, DGI, will carry out import cost controls at the country of origin rather than on Argentine soil.
Customs service head Carlos Silvani has said the new system will put an end to the time-honored practice of "under-billing" -- declaring a lower value on import bills to pay less tariffs.
